Adds a targeted diagnostic suggestion to insert `ref` or remove `ref` when the expected and actual binding types differ only by a reference layer and the binding annotation matches that fix. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Constructs diagnostics suggesting how to rewrite `&`/`&mut` binding patterns into more idiomatic borrowed or mutable binding syntax depending on the enclosing pattern context. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Rejects dereference patterns that would implicitly dereference a trait object binding, emitting E0033 with an explanatory note, and otherwise accepts the pattern as dereferenceable. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks a struct pattern by resolving and validating the struct path, checking the resolved struct type against the expected type, then type-checking and validating the field subpatterns. Calls `check_pat` (when path resolution fails while walking fields), `demand_eqtype_pat`, and `check_struct_pat_fields`.

Type-checks a path pattern that must resolve to a unit constructor or constant: it validates the resolution kind, instantiates the value path, and checks the resulting pattern type against the expected type, emitting a specialized diagnostic on mismatch. Calls `pattern_cause` and `emit_bad_pat_path`.

Detects when a constant used in a pattern was defined from a range literal and, if so, suggests moving that literal directly into the match pattern. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Emits a detailed diagnostic for a path pattern that was interpreted as a constant or item rather than a new binding, labeling the definition site and suggesting fixes such as renaming a struct field binding or rewriting range-like constants. Calls `maybe_suggest_range_literal`.

Type-checks a tuple-struct or tuple-variant pattern by resolving the constructor path, validating that it is a tuple constructor, converting the constructor function type to the constructed ADT type, checking that against the expected type, and then checking each subpattern against its field type. Calls `check_pat`, `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, and `e0023`.

Builds the E0023 diagnostic for tuple-struct/tuple-variant arity mismatches, labeling both the pattern and the definition and producing tailored fix suggestions, including the special case where a single tuple field was mistakenly written as multiple tuple-struct subpatterns. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Type-checks a tuple pattern by synthesizing element type variables, unifying the tuple pattern type with the expected type, and recursively checking each element against its corresponding inferred or error type. Calls `demand_eqtype_pat_diag` and `check_pat`.

Validates and type-checks the fields of a struct pattern: it maps field names to definitions, detects duplicate and nonexistent fields, records field indices, checks field stability and field-pattern types, recursively checks each field subpattern, and enforces rest-pattern/non-exhaustive/union rules. Calls `error_field_already_bound`, `check_pat`, `error_inexistent_fields`, and `error_foreign_non_exhaustive_spat`.

Detects a tuple variant mistakenly written with struct-pattern shorthand fields and returns a diagnostic suggesting the correct tuple-variant pattern syntax. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Emits the error for matching a foreign non-exhaustive struct or variant without `..`, suggesting insertion of `..` at the end of the field list. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.
Emits E0025 when the same field name is bound more than once in a struct pattern, labeling both the repeated and original uses. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Builds the diagnostic for fields named in a struct pattern that do not exist on the matched variant, labeling offending fields and offering typo, tuple-struct, or coercion-based suggestions when possible. It does not call any other method from the provided Methods List.

Detects when a tuple variant is written using struct-pattern syntax and builds E0769 with a tuple-style rewrite suggestion; if the field counts match, it explicitly calls `get_suggested_tuple_struct_pattern` to produce a more precise suggestion.

Constructs the comma-separated replacement text for a tuple-struct pattern by reusing field pattern source snippets when possible and substituting `_` for numeric pseudo-field names that coincide with actual tuple positions.

Emits a diagnostic explaining that a struct pattern must use `..` because some fields are inaccessible, and suggests either appending `, ..` after the last listed field or inserting `{ .. }` for an empty field list.

Lints when a pattern omits fields under `non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns`, formatting the omitted-field list and attaching labels, help, and notes; it explicitly calls the local helper `joined_uncovered_patterns` to summarize omitted field names.
Formats a short human-readable list of omitted identifiers, showing one name, several joined names, or a truncated `and N more` form depending on the number of witnesses.

Builds E0027 for struct patterns that omit required fields, labels the missing fields, and when the pattern shape permits it, suggests inserting explicit missing-field entries plus `..` when inaccessible fields also exist.

Type-checks a `box` pattern by first validating dereferenceability with `check_dereferenceable`, creating an inferred boxed inner type, equating it to the expected type via `demand_eqtype_pat`, and then recursively checking the inner subpattern with `check_pat`.

Type-checks a reference pattern by resolving the expected type, validating dereferenceability with `check_dereferenceable`, reusing an existing reference type or creating one with `new_ref_ty`, enforcing compatibility through `demand_eqtype_pat_diag`, optionally enriching and emitting that diagnostic via `borrow_pat_suggestion`, and finally recursing into the inner pattern with `check_pat`.
Creates a fresh reference type for patterns by allocating a new pattern region variable and returning `&` or `&mut` of the supplied inner type.

For slice patterns without a rest subpattern, attempts to infer a concrete array type by creating a fresh element type variable and pairing it with the fixed pattern length; returns `None` when a variable-length slice pattern is present.
Determines whether the declaration context makes the pattern irrefutable, returning true only for plain local declarations without `else`.

Type-checks slice and array patterns by first resolving the expected type, using `pat_is_irrefutable` and `try_resolve_slice_ty_to_array_ty` to opportunistically infer arrays in irrefutable contexts, dispatching to `check_array_pat_len` for array-length validation, reporting non-array/slice inputs with `error_expected_array_or_slice`, and recursively checking each element and optional rest subpattern with `check_pat`.

Validates an array pattern against a known or inferred array length, evaluating the const length and then either returning an exact/rest slice typing, inferring a fixed-length array with `demand_eqtype`, or reporting length problems via `error_scrutinee_unfixed_length`, `error_scrutinee_inconsistent_length`, or `error_scrutinee_with_rest_inconsistent_length`.
Emits E0527 when a fixed-length array pattern requires a different number of elements than the matched array provides.
Emits E0528 when an array pattern with a rest segment still requires more elements than the matched array contains.
Emits E0730 for attempts to pattern-match on an array whose length is not fixed enough to support the pattern.

Emits E0529 when a slice pattern is applied to a non-array/non-slice input, adds context-sensitive help for reference semantics, probes autoderef chains, and may suggest `.as_deref()` or slicing syntax after consulting `is_slice_or_array_or_vector`.
Classifies whether a type is a slice-like container by recursively peeling references and recognizing `Vec`, slices, and arrays, returning both the boolean result and the resolved underlying type.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/path.rs:: Lowers an AST path plus optional `QSelf` into an HIR `QPath`, using resolver `PartialRes` to split the resolved base from unresolved projections, handling async trait-bound remapping, and constructing either resolved or type-relative path forms. It calls `lower_ty` to lower the `QSelf` type, `lower_res` to convert the base resolution, `map_trait_to_async_trait` when an `async` bound targets an `Fn*` trait, `lower_path_segment` to lower every path segment with the appropriate generic-argument mode, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound spans, `lower_span` for final HIR spans, and `next_id` when synthesizing type-relative HIR nodes.

Lowers an import path into `hir::UsePath`, preserving the provided per-namespace `Res` list and lowering each segment in a context where generic arguments are rejected. It calls `lower_path_segment` for each path segment and `lower_span` for the resulting path span.

Lowers one AST `PathSegment` into an HIR path segment by converting its identifier, resolution, and generic arguments, while diagnosing invalid parenthesized generics, return-type notation misuse, and missing angle brackets. It calls `lower_angle_bracketed_parameter_data` for `<...>` arguments, `lower_parenthesized_parameter_data` for `(...)` function-trait style arguments, `maybe_insert_elided_lifetimes_in_path` to synthesize omitted lifetime arguments when required, `lower_node_id`, `lower_ident`, and `lower_res` to finish the HIR segment, and uses resolver-backed `expect_full_res` to fetch the segment resolution.

Inserts synthesized elided lifetime generic arguments at the front of a path segment when the resolver recorded an elision anchor, choosing a diagnostic span based on whether brackets and other arguments are present. It calls `lower_lifetime` for each generated anonymous lifetime before wrapping them as lifetime generic arguments.

Lowers angle-bracketed generic arguments and associated-item constraints into an intermediate `GenericArgsCtor`, while also reporting whether the arguments are effectively elidable in optional-parameter mode. It calls `lower_generic_arg` for each non-constraint generic argument and `lower_assoc_item_constraint` for each associated-item constraint.

Lowers parenthesized function-trait-style generic arguments by turning inputs into a tuple argument and the return type into an `Output` associated type constraint, while enforcing the allowed `impl Trait` contexts and propagating async-bound feature tagging. It calls `lower_ty_direct` to lower input types, `lower_ty` to lower the return type under the correct `ImplTraitContext`, `ty_tup` to build tuple types for inputs or default unit output, `mark_span_with_reason` to tag desugared async-bound output spans, and `assoc_ty_binding` to create the synthetic `Output = ...` constraint.

Builds an HIR associated-type equality constraint like `Output = T` with empty generic arguments and fresh HIR identity data. It calls `next_id` to allocate the constraint HIR id and `lower_span` to lower the source span.

Maps the lang-item `Fn`, `FnMut`, or `FnOnce` trait `DefId` to its corresponding async function-trait lang item, returning `None` for all other traits. It does not call other methods from the listed methods set.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ast_lowering/src/pat.rs::: Allocates and returns the HIR form of an AST pattern. It calls `lower_pat_mut` to perform the actual lowering and then stores the result with arena allocation.

Main pattern-lowering worker that matches each AST `PatKind` and builds the corresponding HIR pattern, using an iterative loop for parenthesized patterns and stack protection for deep inputs. It calls `lower_pat_ident` for identifier bindings, `lower_expr_within_pat` for literal/range endpoints, `lower_qpath` for path-like patterns, `lower_pat_tuple` for tuple and tuple-struct elements, `lower_pat_slice` for slice patterns, `lower_pat` and `lower_pat_mut` recursively for subpatterns, `lower_node_id`, `lower_attrs`, `lower_ident`, and `lower_span` when constructing struct-field patterns, `lower_range_end` for range syntax, `ban_illegal_rest_pat` for misplaced `..`, and `pat_with_node_id_of` to rebuild the final HIR node with the original ids/spans.

Lowers tuple-like pattern element lists and computes the single valid `..` position for tuple or tuple-struct patterns. It calls `lower_pat_mut` to lower ordinary element patterns and `ban_extra_rest_pat` to diagnose repeated rest patterns, while also emitting an error for illegal bound sub-tuple rests.

Lowers slice/array patterns by splitting elements into leading patterns, one optional subslice, and trailing patterns, converting `binding @ ..` into `binding @ _` to keep HIR valid. It calls `pat_wild_with_node_id_of`, `lower_pat_ident`, and `pat_with_node_id_of` when rewriting subslice bindings, `lower_pat_mut` for normal element patterns, and `ban_extra_rest_pat` when more than one rest/subslice pattern appears.

Lowers an identifier pattern by consulting name resolution to distinguish a local binding from a resolved path/constructor. For bindings it calls `lower_node_id`, `lower_ident`, and the provided `lower_sub` closure; for resolved names it calls `lower_res`, `next_id`, `lower_span`, and `lower_ident` to build a resolved `QPath`.
Creates an allocated wildcard HIR pattern that preserves the source pattern's node id and span. It calls `pat_with_node_id_of` to build the pattern and then arena-allocates it.
Constructs a HIR pattern with a supplied `PatKind` while preserving the original AST pattern identity metadata. It calls `lower_node_id` and `lower_span` to transfer the source pattern's id and span.
Emits the diagnostic for a second `..` rest pattern in a list context such as tuples or slices. It calls `dcx().emit_err` with `ExtraDoubleDot`.
Diagnoses a misplaced `..` pattern outside a valid list context and recovers by lowering it as a wildcard. It calls `dcx().emit_err` with `MisplacedDoubleDot` and returns `hir::PatKind::Wild`.
Converts an AST range-end marker into the corresponding HIR `RangeEnd`, treating missing ends as included so `X..` behaves like a from-range. It does not call other methods in this file.

Validates that an expression used inside a pattern is one of the restricted allowed forms and lowers it to HIR. It calls `dcx().emit_err` and `expr_err` to report and recover from arbitrary expressions, and otherwise calls `lower_expr` to produce the final HIR expression.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/astconv/: Builds and emits the diagnostic for a provided generic argument whose kind does not match the expected parameter kind, adding targeted suggestions for const/type confusion, missing const braces, `_` const inference, and likely ordering mistakes. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Constructs the full `GenericArgsRef` for `def_id` and its generic parents by walking the parent chain, reusing `parent_args`, inserting implicit `Self`, consuming explicit path arguments from the context, inferring omitted arguments, and preserving parameter order. When an explicit argument kind does not match the current parameter, it calls `generic_arg_mismatch_err` to report the mismatch before continuing argument assembly.

Adapts call-site path segments into generic-argument count checking by selecting empty args when absent, choosing the correct `GenericArgPosition` for method vs value calls, computing whether `Self` is implicit, and then calling `check_generic_arg_count` to perform the actual validation.

Validates the number and placement of lifetime, type, and const generic arguments for a path segment, accounting for defaults, synthetic parameters, inferred lifetimes, explicit late-bound lifetimes, and associated type bindings, while collecting invalid spans and emitting structured diagnostics for mismatches. It calls `prohibit_explicit_late_bound_lifetimes` to detect/report forbidden explicit late-bound lifetime arguments.

Checks whether explicit lifetime arguments are forbidden because the target generics contain late-bound regions, allowing implicit inference cases, and otherwise emits either a hard error or lint depending on the argument position and count. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
Required trait hook that returns the `TyCtxt` used by AST-to-type conversion. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that returns the current item `DefId` for the conversion context. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that retrieves generic predicates/bounds for a type parameter or associated item lookup context. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that supplies an inferred or fallback region for omitted/invalid lifetime arguments. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that creates an inferred type argument for an omitted type parameter. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that reports whether `_` type inference syntax is permitted in the current conversion context. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that creates an inferred const argument for an omitted or inferred const generic. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that computes the projected associated type from a polymorphic trait reference and path segment. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that probes whether a type corresponds to an ADT and returns its definition if so. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that marks the conversion context as tainted by a previously emitted error. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that records the resolved type for a HIR node. It does not call other methods in this file.
Default helper that coerces `self` to `&dyn AstConv<'tcx>` for object-style access. It does not call other methods in this file.
Required trait hook that exposes the optional inference context backing AST conversion. It does not call other methods in this file.

Converts a HIR lifetime into a semantic `ty::Region` by resolving named bound variables, early-bound parameters, free regions, and error cases, and falls back to inference or an error region for unresolved elided lifetimes. This method explicitly calls `tcx` and `re_infer`.

Builds instantiated generic arguments for a type path segment and rejects associated type bindings in plain type position before returning the resulting `GenericArgsRef`. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path` and `tcx`.

Core generic-argument instantiation routine for a path: it validates generic arity, handles parent and `Self` arguments, and constructs substitutions by combining explicit HIR arguments with defaults or inference through the local `SubstsForAstPathCtxt` helper. This method explicitly calls `tcx`.

Builds instantiated generic arguments for an associated item path using inherited parent arguments, then rejects associated type bindings in this plain associated-item argument position. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_path` and `tcx`.

Creates a monomorphic trait reference from a parsed trait path and explicit `Self` type after first forbidding generics on all non-final path segments. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`.

Top-level entry point for instantiating a parsed trait bound into polymorphic bounds data: it extracts the final path segment, rejects generics on earlier segments, checks for internal `Fn`-trait diagnostics, and delegates the actual construction to `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`. This method explicitly calls `prohibit_generics`, `complain_about_internal_fn_trait`, and `instantiate_poly_trait_ref_inner`.

Builds a non-polymorphic `ty::TraitRef` from a trait path segment and `Self` type by first creating trait arguments and then rejecting associated type bindings in this context. This method explicitly calls `create_args_for_ast_trait_ref` and `tcx`.

Constructs generic arguments for a trait reference path, after first issuing diagnostics for internal `Fn`-trait usage, by delegating to the general path-argument builder with the supplied `Self` type. This method explicitly calls `complain_about_internal_fn_trait` and `create_args_for_ast_path`.
Checks whether a trait defines an associated item of the given kind and name by querying `tcx().associated_items(...)`, calling `find_by_name_and_kind`, and returning whether the result `is_some()`.

Converts a resolved type path into a `Ty` by first calling `ast_path_args_for_ty` to build generic arguments, then either constructing a lazy type-alias `Ty::new_alias` when `def_kind`/`type_alias_is_lazy` indicate a lazy alias, or instantiating `tcx.at(span).type_of(did)` with those args.

Builds and emits the E0223 ambiguous-associated-type diagnostic, checking `tcx().resolutions(())` for the std-module confusion case and otherwise assembling context-sensitive suggestions with `span_suggestion_verbose` or `span_suggestions` before `emit()`.

Finds the unique trait bound on a type parameter that defines a named associated item by calling `get_type_parameter_bounds` to collect predicates and then delegating to `one_bound_for_assoc_type`, supplying candidates produced from `traits::transitive_bounds_that_define_assoc_item`.

Resolves a type-relative path like `T::Assoc` by first probing ADTs with `probe_adt` to detect enum variants or inherent associated types, using `prohibit_generics` for invalid variant generics, then calling `lookup_inherent_assoc_ty` for inherent associated types or `one_bound_for_assoc_type` over trait/supertrait candidates to produce the final associated type, while also performing stability and diagnostic handling through `tcx` queries.

Searches inherent impls of an ADT for an applicable inherent associated type: it gathers raw candidates by calling `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked`, then uses an inference context and normalization/obligation checking to filter applicable impls, and finally instantiates the selected associated type with `fresh_args_for_item`, `type_of`, and `instantiate`.
Looks up an associated type in a scope by calling `lookup_assoc_ty_unchecked`, validating the result with `check_assoc_ty`, and returning the associated item `DefId` if found.

Performs unchecked associated-type lookup in a scope by adjusting the identifier with `tcx.adjust_ident_and_get_scope`, scanning `tcx.associated_items(scope).in_definition_order()`, and returning the matching type-namespace item together with the resolved scope.
Verifies that an associated type is accessible and stable by checking `tcx.visibility(item).is_accessible_from(...)`, emitting a privacy error if needed, and then calling `tcx.check_stability`.

Finds accessible traits whose associated types could match a given `qself_ty` by scanning `tcx.all_traits()`, filtering traits with a matching associated type in `associated_items`, checking visibility, and testing impl self-types for unification with an inference context before collecting trait path strings.

Converts a qualified path `<Self as Trait>::Assoc` into a projection type; when `Self` is omitted it gathers candidate implementing type names and calls `report_ambiguous_associated_type` to emit an error, otherwise it builds the trait ref with `ast_path_to_mono_trait_ref`, creates item args with `create_args_for_associated_item`, and returns `Ty::new_projection`.

Rejects generic arguments and associated type bindings on path segments that must not have them: it scans the segments’ args to classify forbidden lifetime/type/const/infer arguments, emits a tailored diagnostic through the supplied `extend` callback, and calls `prohibit_assoc_ty_binding` for associated type bindings.

Reconstructs which path segments in a value path carry generic arguments by analyzing the resolved `DefKind`, querying `tcx.generics_of`, and in ADT-related cases using `probe_adt`/parent relationships to produce a sequence of `PathSeg` entries describing the relevant definition and segment index.

Converts a resolved HIR path into a type by dispatching on `path.res`: it calls `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_args_for_ty` for opaque types, `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for ordinary nominal types, `def_ids_for_value_path_segments` plus `prohibit_generics` and `ast_path_to_ty` for variant paths, `associated_path_to_ty` for type-relative paths, and `hir_id_to_bound_ty` for type parameters, while also emitting diagnostics for invalid resolutions.

Converts a HIR id for a bound type parameter into a `Ty` by querying `tcx.named_bound_var`: late-bound parameters become `Ty::new_bound`, early-bound parameters use `hir().ty_param_owner` plus `generics_of` to build `Ty::new_param`, and error resolutions become `Ty::new_error`.

Converts a HIR id for a bound const parameter into a `Const` by querying `tcx.named_bound_var`: early-bound parameters use `parent` and `generics_of` to build `Const::new_param`, late-bound parameters become `Const::new_bound`, and error resolutions become `Const::new_error`.
Converts a HIR type into a semantic type by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with the default non-borrowed, non-path flags.
Converts a HIR type appearing inside a path by calling `ast_ty_to_ty_inner` with `in_path` enabled.

Core recursive HIR-type conversion routine. It converts slices, pointers, refs, tuples, bare fns, trait objects, paths, opaque defs, and type-relative paths by calling other helpers such as `ast_ty_to_ty`, `ast_region_to_region`, `ty_of_fn`, `maybe_lint_bare_trait`, `conv_object_ty_poly_trait_ref`, `res_to_ty`, `impl_trait_ty_to_ty`, and `associated_path_to_ty`, then constructs the corresponding `Ty` node.

Builds the type for an `impl Trait`/opaque definition by iterating the item generics, resolving explicit lifetime arguments with `ast_region_to_region`, filling other parameters from `mk_param_from_def`, and then returning either `Ty::new_projection` for trait context or `Ty::new_opaque` otherwise.
Computes an argument type, reusing an expected type for `_` arguments by calling `record_ty`, and otherwise delegating to `ast_ty_to_ty`.

Constructs a function signature from HIR by collecting late-bound vars, walking generics for placeholder detection, converting inputs with `ty_of_arg`, converting the return type with `ast_ty_to_ty` when present, building the signature with `mk_fn_sig`/`bind_with_vars`, optionally calling `suggest_trait_fn_ty_for_impl_fn_infer` for `_` recovery, and finally validating region usage with `validate_late_bound_regions` after computing constrained and referenced late-bound regions.

When an impl method uses `_` in its signature, tries to recover the corresponding trait method type by computing the impl’s trait ref with `instantiate_mono_trait_ref` and `ast_ty_to_ty`, locating the associated method via `associated_items(...).find_by_name_and_kind`, instantiating its `fn_sig`, liberating late-bound regions, and returning the requested input or output type.

Checks that every referenced late-bound region is constrained by iterating `referenced_regions.difference(&constrained_regions)`, creating each diagnostic with `generate_err`, adding explanatory notes for anonymous lifetimes, and emitting the error.

Computes the lifetime bound for a trait object from its existential predicates when no explicit bound is given. It calls `tcx` to access the type context and `object_region_bounds` to derive candidate region bounds; if the derived set `is_empty`, it returns `None` so the caller can use the default. It then uses `iter`/`any` together with `is_static` to prefer `'static` when present, and otherwise checks whether all derived bounds are the same; if multiple distinct bounds exist, it calls `emit_err` to report an ambiguous lifetime bound before returning one of the derived regions.

Trait hook that supplies the explicit generic arguments associated with a given definition id, along with whether argument inference is enabled. This declaration does not call other Methods List methods.

Trait hook that converts a syntactically provided generic argument into an internal `ty::GenericArg` for the corresponding generic parameter. This declaration does not call other Methods List methods.
Trait hook that creates an inferred or defaulted internal generic argument when no explicit argument is supplied. This declaration does not call other Methods List methods.

Returns this path context's stored generic arguments only when the queried `DefId` matches the path's target definition; otherwise returns no arguments and disables inference. It does not call other Methods List methods.

Converts an explicit lifetime, type, inferred type placeholder, or const generic argument into the corresponding internal generic argument, while enforcing stability for defaults, rejecting disallowed `_` type inference, and seeding anonymous const types. It explicitly calls `ast_region_to_region` for lifetime arguments.

Builds a missing generic argument by inferring a lifetime/type/const, using a declared default when permitted, or producing an error placeholder during recovery. It does not call other Methods List methods.

Selects the unique trait bound that defines a requested associated item, reporting either absence or ambiguity and enriching ambiguity diagnostics with candidate-bound suggestions. It explicitly calls `assoc_kind_str` to format the associated item kind in diagnostics.

Filters inherent associated type candidates by probing whether each impl's self type and obligations can match the requested self type, then returns the unique applicable candidate or reports none/ambiguity. It does not call other Methods List methods.

Validates that a delegated function signature is supported by rejecting recursive delegation, opaque returns, early-bound generics, async/const/variadic/unsafe/non-Rust-ABI callees, optionally emitting diagnostics and returning whether any violation was found. It does not call other Methods List methods.

Computes the delegated input or output type for a signature, first checking whether delegation is allowed and then instantiating the callee signature, including substituting the impl self type when needed. It explicitly calls `check_delegation_constraints`.
Maps an associated item kind enum to its user-facing string label (`function`, `constant`, or `type`). It does not call other Methods List methods.

Type-checks an expression with a type hint by calling `check_expr_with_hint`, then coerces the result to the expected type with `demand_coerce` without two-phase borrowing.
A thin helper that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with `ExpectHasType(expected)` to type-check an expression using a concrete expected type as a hint.
Checks an expression by calling `check_expr_with_expectation`, and if the usage requires a mutable place, calls `convert_place_derefs_to_mutable` to upgrade deref adjustments accordingly.
Default expression entry point that calls `check_expr_with_expectation` with no expectation.
Checks an expression with place/mutability requirements by calling `check_expr_with_expectation_and_needs` with no type expectation.
Main convenience wrapper that forwards expression checking to `check_expr_with_expectation_and_args` with no call arguments or enclosing call expression.

Core expression-checking entry point that handles logging, unreachable-code and divergence bookkeeping, then dispatches path expressions to `check_expr_path` and all other expression forms to `check_expr_kind`, finally resolving the resulting type for recording and diagnostics.

Dispatches each HIR expression kind to its specialized checker, including `check_lit`, `check_binop`, `check_expr_assign`, `check_binop_assign`, `check_expr_unary`, `check_expr_addr_of`, `check_lang_item_path`, `check_expr_path`, `check_expr_asm`, `check_offset_of`, `check_expr_break`, `check_expr_return`, `check_expr_become`, `check_expr_let`, `check_expr_loop`, and `check_match`.
